rules.statement: A Helm chart's values must never hold a secret; database, cache, key and other credentials are referenced by the name of an existing Secret (or ConfigMap for public material) that the operator creates.
rules.why: Values files are committed, sometimes to public repositories, so a chart that accepts a secret value invites leaking it.
rules.check: Look for values keys or template code that take a password, connection string, key or token as a literal value instead of an `existingSecret`-style reference.

rules.statement: A Helm chart refuses at render time (via `fail` or `required`) any configuration the application would reject at startup, instead of rendering it and leaving a pod in a crash loop.
rules.why: Failing the render means `helm install` applies nothing and the operator learns of the unsafe release before anything is deployed.
rules.check: For each new or changed setting that the application validates at startup (empty or wildcard hosts, missing required Secret, both-and-neither alternatives, replicas above 1 without shared state, non-https authority), check that the templates have a matching render-time failure.

rules.statement: A Helm chart ships a `values.schema.json` that rejects unknown and mistyped values, and adds each new value to it.
rules.why: A typo should fail the install instead of being silently ignored.
rules.check: Check that new values keys appear in values.schema.json with a type, and that objects set `additionalProperties: false`.

rules.statement: Every render-time refusal added to a chart comes with a CI case showing that the unsafe release fails to render, and every supported release under `ci/` must render under `helm lint --strict`.
rules.why: CI checks the contract, so a change that lets an unsafe release render fails the build.
rules.check: When a diff adds or changes a `fail`/`required` check, look for a matching failing-release fixture and the workflow step that asserts it fails.

rules.statement: A Deployment whose replicas keep single-use state in process uses the `Recreate` strategy, and it uses a rolling update with `maxSurge: 1` and `maxUnavailable: 0` only when that state is in a shared store.
rules.why: Two replicas with in-process single-use state must never run at once, and a rolling update with `maxSurge: 0` still starts the new pod while the old one serves.
rules.check: Check that the strategy template switches on whether a shared state store is configured, and look for rolling updates (including `maxSurge: 0`) used without one.

rules.statement: Chart pods meet the restricted Pod Security Standard: they run as a non-root UID, drop all capabilities, set `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, use the `RuntimeDefault` seccomp profile, have a read-only root filesystem with an `emptyDir` for `/tmp`, and don't mount a service-account token.
rules.why: The chart has to run the hardened image under restricted pod security.
rules.check: Inspect pod and container securityContext and `automountServiceAccountToken` in each workload template, and flag anything missing or loosened.

rules.statement: Secret volumes in a chart mount with mode `0440` and are readable through `fsGroup`, not world-readable.
rules.why: Secret files should be readable only by the app's user and group.
rules.check: Check `defaultMode` on secret volumes and the pod's `fsGroup`.

rules.statement: Each chart component gets its own ServiceAccount and doesn't reuse another component's.
rules.why: Another component's ServiceAccount may carry cloud identities this component must not have.
rules.check: Look for a workload template that refers to another component's ServiceAccount name.

rules.statement: Probes for an HTTPS-only ASP.NET Core pod use `scheme: HTTPS` and send a `Host` header that `AllowedHosts` accepts; startup and liveness probes call the liveness endpoint and only readiness calls the readiness endpoint.
rules.why: The kubelet sends the pod IP as Host, which AllowedHosts rejects. Liveness must not check dependencies, but readiness does.
rules.check: Inspect probe definitions for scheme, an httpHeaders Host entry that isn't a wildcard, and which health path each probe uses.

rules.statement: A terminating pod keeps serving for a short drain through a `preStop` kubelet `sleep` action, and that drain fits within `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`.
rules.why: The endpoint has to leave load balancers before the process stops, so in-flight traffic isn't dropped.
rules.check: Check that a preStop sleep is present and that its duration plus shutdown time is less than the grace period.

rules.statement: A Helm chart lives outside any .NET project directory, so the Web SDK's content globs and the image build context never pick up its files.
rules.why: Chart files inside a project directory would be swept into the published output or the Docker build context.
rules.check: Look for chart directories added under a folder that contains a .csproj or under a Docker build context.
